title: Recipe and Yearbook
premise: Xanthe Crane has survived high school by staying invisible, pouring everything she can't say into the bread she bakes at her family's struggling bakery. When her English teacher pairs her with Marisol Vega — her former best friend turned rival — for a semester project documenting 'a community recipe,' Xanthe is forced to work alongside the one person who knows exactly why she went quiet. As their recipe book grows into a confession of shared history, a final audition for a citywide youth culinary showcase forces both girls to choose between protecting old wounds and telling the truth that could cost them each other. In the end, Xanthe bakes the truth into a single loaf, loses the competition but wins back something rarer: a friendship rebuilt on honesty and a found family of misfits who taste what she's been trying to say all along.
about_author: L. M. Reyes grew up above a panadería in a rust-belt town where every celebration smelled like yeast and sugar. A former line cook turned teacher, they write stories about kids who find family in the unlikeliest kitchens.

chapters.title: The Quiet Loaf
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet her kneading grief and silence into sourdough before dawn at Crane's Bakery, then navigating school with practiced invisibility. Establishes her rule: head down, grades up, locker shut. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: Assigned Seats
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Mr. Okafor announces the semester project: pairs must document a community recipe and present it at the spring showcase. He assigns Xanthe with Marisol Vega, her ex-best friend who hasn't spoken to her in two years. Emotional beat: dread; the past walks back in wearing a name tag.

chapters.title: What Marisol Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced to interview each other about family recipes, Marisol reveals her mother left last year, and her abuela's tamales are the only thread holding her together. Xanthe realizes Marisol's coldness was grief, not hatred. Emotional beat: reluctant empathy cracking old ice.

chapters.title: Flour Wars
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The girls clash over whose recipe represents 'community' — Marisol's tamalada or Xanthe's bread. Their argument spills into the hallway, drawing an audience. Xanthe retreats to the bakery, where Dad admits they may lose the lease. Emotional beat: stakes multiply; home itself is fragile.

chapters.title: The Misfit Table
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Project interviews pull in cafeteria outcasts: Dev, who codes recipes for his diabetic sister; Priya, who translates her grandmother's handwritten cards. They start gathering at the bakery after hours. Emotional beat: belonging sneaks up on her; found family begins forming around flour and sugar.

chapters.title: Two Years Ago
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, flashback woven through present. We learn the rupture: Xanthe stayed silent when Marisol was humiliated at freshman showcase, choosing her scholarship audition over defending her friend. Marisol confesses she never stopped waiting for an apology. Emotional beat: the wound finally named.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The recipe book becomes a sensation at school; the misfit table grows. But the showcase committee announces live auditions — meaning Xanthe and Marisol must co-present on stage. Meanwhile the bakery gets an eviction notice dated the week of auditions. Emotional beat: hope and pressure rising like overproofed dough.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Rehearsals implode when Xanthe's father forbids her from missing bakery shifts, and Marisol accuses her of abandoning everything — again. Xanthe, cornered, says the cruelest true thing: 'You never gave me room to be anything but perfect.' Both walk away. Emotional beat: rock bottom; the friendship looks truly dead.

chapters.title: The Truth Loaf
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The night before auditions, Xanthe bakes a loaf embedded with the whole story — burnt edges for the silence, honey for what she should have said — and brings it to Marisol's door. She apologizes without excuses. Marisol doesn't forgive her yet, but shows up at the audition anyway. Emotional beat: costly honesty; forgiveness left deliberately unfinished.

chapters.title: Recipe and Yearbook
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On stage, the girls abandon their polished script and tell the true story — the fight, the silence, the bread — while the misfit table holds up the finished recipe book like a yearbook of everyone who fed them. They don't win first place, but a local chef offers the bakery a partnership that saves it. Final beat: Xanthe signs Marisol's yearbook with a new recipe — one for starting over.
